# Live link checks on a fresh OpenPhish sample

*Eval date 2026-10-22. Generated by `scripts/eval_live_links.py`. **Edition 4 (2026-10-23, decision C3):** the app now applies the validation-picked URL flag threshold (e), the exact-brand rule R10 and nine more hosting platforms; section 10 compares (b), (e) and the three together. **Edition 3 (decision C2):** variant (b) is now the app's rule, the maintained shortener list is merged in, and the age-gate and threshold variants (d), (e), (d)+(e) are scored (section 10, not applied to the app). Edition 2 (decision C1) re-scored the same sample and cached replies offline after the platform lists, the gambling additions and the crt.sh switch changed; edition 1 (commit 231db07) is the "before" of section 9. Sample and cached replies: `data/eval_live/`. Re-run: `.venv/bin/python scripts/eval_live_links.py --date 2026-10-22 --offline`.*

> **Read this first.** The "after" numbers were tuned on this same 96 + 200 + 22 link sample, so they are optimistic and must be confirmed on a fresh pull (a separate task). The URL-model variants and the C3 changes of section 10 are also scored on it: the exact-brand rule and the platform additions were written after reading the list of scams that (e) loses, so their recovery is by construction. Only the threshold of (e) comes from outside the sample (the URL head's validation split).

## Summary

1. **Phishing, honest setting** (OpenPhish, URLhaus and Tranco switched off): of 96 fresh OpenPhish links (one per registered domain; the feed held only 96 such domains, not 200) the app flagged 72 (75% [65-83]), 35 of them as Likely scam; 4 were rated "No warning signs" and 20 "Can't judge" (free hosting / shorteners). With all signals ON it flags 100%, which is mostly the app finding its own source list.
2. **Benign, honest setting:** 9% [5-16] of 100 Tranco top-10k domains and 20% [13-29] of 100 domains ranked 100k-1M were flagged Suspicious or Likely scam (95% intervals in brackets). The top-10k figure is what you get when Tranco is off; with Tranco on it is 0%, which is circular because the benign domains came from Tranco.
3. **Known gambling miss:** the original spam-ad link was never recorded, so it cannot be replayed. For the 8 gambling sites BUGS.md says the lookup misses (all Tranco top 10k), 0 are rated "No warning signs" with Tranco ON and 0 with it OFF: no longer rated safe (section f).

## 1. What was measured

**Function judged:** `shield.core.router.analyse(text, text_model, url_model, live=True)` followed by `shield.core.report.to_report(text, r)`, exactly what `POST /api/analyse` runs (`src/shield/api/main.py`). Text head: `MurilScorer`. Each sampled link is the whole message, so the text head is skipped and the verdict is the link verdict. The verdict is `Report.level`; "flagged" = Likely scam or Suspicious.

**Phishing set (96 links).** OpenPhish public feed, downloaded 2026-10-22T20:53:47+00:00 (SHA-256 `7f1d3bd7ed0cdbcf…`), 300 URLs, 96 unique registered domains (`tldextract.top_domain_under_public_suffix`, which is the same value as the app's `link_domain` for all 96 links). **The target was 200; the feed cannot give more** because 196 of its 300 URLs are pages on free-hosting / user-content platforms (pages.dev alone is one registered domain). All 96 were taken. By kind of host: free_hosting 13, own_domain 83. **Only 83 are ordinary domains** with registry and DNS facts; for the 13 platform-hosted or shortened links the app looks up neither (the registration of pages.dev says nothing about the page), so domain age, certificate age and DNS cannot fire on them by design.

**Benign set (200 domains).** Tranco list on disk (2026-10-22), 100 random domains from ranks 1-10,000 and 100 from 100,000-1,000,000, one `hxxps://<domain>/` each, none also in another set. Skipped before sampling: top 10k: 55 platform / shortener / user content (judged by other rules), 30 already in another set; 100k-1M: 9 already in another set, 3 platform / shortener / user content (judged by other rules). Tranco is not a list of verified-good sites (the 100k-1M band contains some hosting, adult, gambling and a few abusive sites), so a few "false alarms" there can be correct.

**Regression group (22 domains + 3 messages).** Described in section f.

**Not measured / not on:** Google Safe Browsing (no `SAFE_BROWSING_KEY`, so the app skips it), shortener expansion (never run), the sender rule. The URLhaus list is the 30-day export. Samples are only strings: no link was fetched, resolved or connected to (section 8).

**crt.sh certificate-age check (R8):** OFF, the new default (decision C1) in this run. The cached replies of edition 1 still hold the 68 crt.sh requests (section 8 describes them); with the check off the app sends none, so the certificate rows of section 2 are empty and R8 cannot fire.

**Lifted limits (so the throttle does not fake failures):** the 4 s message deadline of `live.run` is 60 s here; per-call timeout stays 2 s (`net.CALL_TIMEOUT`). RDAP / crt.sh failures were retried twice; the "first attempt only" row below uses the first try of every call, which is what the app does.

RDAP outcomes (ordinary domains only): phishing: date 60, unsupported 15, failed:timeout 1; benign top 10k: date 78, unsupported 20, failed:http_301 1; benign 100k-1M: date 76, unsupported 24. `unsupported` = the TLD has no public RDAP service in IANA's bootstrap file; `no_date` = the registry answered without a registration event; `not_found` = the registry has no such name.

DNS names that no longer resolve (NXDOMAIN): phishing 11 of 83 ordinary domains, benign top 10k 0, benign 100k-1M 0.

Other offline signals that fired (all-ON): homograph R3: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200; brand lookalike R4: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200; raw IP R5: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200; two or more red flags R9: phishing 0/96, benign 0/200. URL model (host-only head) rated Suspicious or higher before the link checks: phishing 67 of 96 at score >= 0.5 (for orientation only; the app's cut-offs are in `models/url_head.joblib`).

## 7. (f) Regression group: gambling / spam-ad links

**The reported link is not available.** BUGS.md says the exact message "was never supplied", so "a spam-ad link that led to a gambling site was rated safe" cannot be replayed. If you have the link or message, add it to `UNLISTED` / `MESSAGES` in the script and rerun. What is tested instead, from what the repo documents: `unlisted` = gambling sites BUGS.md names as missing from the gambling lookup; `unconfirmed` = the 4 gambling-looking domains still `pending_review`; `control` = domains the lookup lists (G1 must say Suspicious); `message` = spam-ad text with a gambling link in the three forms the problem could take. **Result.** Unlisted gambling sites rated "No warning signs": 0 of 8 with all signals ON, 0 of 8 in the honest setting. Unconfirmed: 4 of 4 / 4 of 4. Controls flagged: 10 of 10 (all ON), 10 of 10 (honest). Reading it: P2 ("a well-known website") is on every unlisted top-10k site in the all-ON run, but switching Tranco off still leaves 0 of 8 at "No warning signs", so P2 is not the cause: nothing in the URL model or the link checks knows these sites are gambling sites; only the gambling lookup does. In the message cases the verdict comes from the text head reading the ad wording, not from the link.

Same links, same cached replies, same honest setting (OpenPhish, URLhaus and Tranco off) with the pre-C2 URL rule (a), so only the list changes show here (the app has used (b) since C2: section 10). ## 10. URL-model variants and the C3 changes (honest setting)

> **Same-sample warning.** These numbers come from the same 96 + 200 links that the changes of C1, C2 and C3 were looked at on: the exact-brand rule and the platform additions were written after reading the list of scams that (e) loses, so they recover those scams by construction. They must be confirmed on a fresh pull (a separate task). Differences of 1-3 links are inside the noise of 96 / 100 links.

Honest setting = OpenPhish, URLhaus and Tranco off. The URL model alone is capped at Suspicious in every row (decision C2). **(b)** = the app before C3 (flag threshold 0.537). **(e)** = flag threshold 0.662, picked on the URL head's own validation split (decision C3, now in the app). **(e) + R10 + platforms** = the app since C3: R10 is the exact-brand-name rule (`lookalike.exact_brand`: the registered domain's first label equals a brand's label but the domain is not in the brand's official list; Suspicious, no substring or fuzzy match), and nine more hosting platforms are in `platforms.py` (edgeone.dev, 4everland.app, azurestaticapps.net, cloudworkstations.dev, crabdance.com, flazio.online, typedream.app, teleporthq.app as free hosting; backblazeb2.com as user content). Each piece is switched on in this script only for the rows that name it.

The remaining hits in the top 100k are left flagged: they are other TLDs of Roblox, Zomato, Blinkit, BharatPe and `amazon.work`, whose ownership cannot be told from the name alone, and checking would need a registry look-up (a network call). If one of them is the brand's own, the effect is a Suspicious flag with the sentence "Uses the name X but is not X's official website" on a link to a defensive registration, and the fix is one line in the official list. `reports/exact_brand_scan.md` has the full list.
